A.explanation: Wavelength $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ is $5000 \text{ nm}$, which is in the infrared region beyond the visible $400-700 \text{ nm}$ range, so it is invisible.

B.explanation: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in free space (vacuum).

C.explanation: Electromagnetic waves are transverse oscillating electric and magnetic fields, so they can be polarised.

D.explanation: They consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields, not vibrating atoms, and can travel through vacuum.

hints: Recall the approximate limits of human vision in metres or nanometres and convert $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ to nanometres to compare.
Recall what speed all parts of the electromagnetic spectrum share in free space, and whether that speed depends on wavelength.
Recall whether electromagnetic waves are transverse or longitudinal and what vibrating atoms would imply about needing a medium.
walkthrough: Note the test wavelength $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m} = 5000 \text{ nm}$ and recall visible light is only about $400 \text{ nm}$ to $700 \text{ nm}$, or $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Since $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ is about ten times larger than red light, it lies in the infrared region, which the human eye cannot detect.
Check the other statements against EM wave properties: all EM waves travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in free space, so speed does not differ with wavelength.
EM waves are transverse, so they can be polarised, and they are oscillating electric and magnetic fields that need no medium, not vibrations of atoms.
Therefore only the statement about invisibility of the $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ wave follows. This is option A
